header_addition:
/* Distinct V8/Node continuation-preserved data, never the application
   execution_context capability token. Get returns one owned value. Set borrows
   value, duplicates/publishes it before old-root retirement, performs no guest
   property operation, and preserves the first actual pending/fatal completion.
   These native operations remain available during pending/disallowed cleanup.
   A nonempty Node checkpoint saves the outer value, sets undefined once, runs
   jobs, then restores before completed callbacks. Individual successful jobs
   clear the slot; failed jobs retain it; an undefined job capture skips setup.
   Empty/disallowed JS_ExecutePendingJob calls do not touch the slot or queue.
   Runtime/job references are counted external GC roots; Promise reaction
   references are marked as part of the actual Promise graph. */
JS_EXTERN JSValue JS_PiGetContinuationPreservedEmbedderData(JSRuntime *rt);
JS_EXTERN void JS_PiSetContinuationPreservedEmbedderData(JSRuntime *rt,
                                                         JSValueConst value);
reversal: All sixteen original replacements plus the one bounded reaction-retirement successor reverse in reverse order to the complete prior C; removal of the header addition reverses the complete prior H. The two original reaction enqueue sites are one explicitly counted replacement.
ownership_contract: Get returns one owned root; Set borrows and publishes its duplicate before prior-root retirement.
Only actual pending reasons participate in the native root-retirement reducer; a flagged continuation DATA value does not create an event.
Runtime and native job roots are externally counted references in the existing QuickJS cycle collector; the actual Promise reaction gc_mark includes its new edge.
Existing capability root captures and context-hook code remain in place; continuation data is a distinct field.
No outer value is restored per job. Root's actual nonempty checkpoint performs one save/reset and restores before completed callbacks; empty/disallowed C job calls do not touch the slot.
Successful tasks clear; failed tasks retain; undefined captures skip setup. Ordinary handler rejection contained by the real Promise reaction still completes its task normally.
Existing job root order remains capability, then new continuation capture, original argv in order, and returned result. Actual pending is retained across those releases.

This slot unit does not itself implement Node exception reporting, termination queue clearing, checkpoint completion callbacks or the async_context_frame option gate; those remain the actual Environment caller boundary.
